在已有授权签发、单次消费、紧急撤销、授权使用记录和执行回执的基线上，我需要新增 POST /machines/{machine_id}/authorization-grants/batch-consume，让自动化执行器一次确认多项授权的使用，并保证整批成功或整批不变。请求体只接受 {"grant_ids":[...]}，数组按输入顺序包含 1 到 100 个裁剪后非空且不重复的字符串。成功时按输入顺序返回 [{grant_id, use_id, consumed_at}, ...]，use_id 为每项新生成的消费记录标识，consumed_at 为整批共同的 UTC 提交时刻并以 Z 结束，每个授权只生成一条使用记录。

错误体沿用 {"error":{"code":"<code>"}}。任何查询参数返回 422 invalid_query 且优先于机器不存在；请求形状错误、数组越界、元素类型错误、裁剪后为空或 grant_id 重复返回 422 invalid_grant_request，所有校验先于数据库读取。校验后，机器不存在、授权不存在或授权属于其他机器均返回 404 not_found。逐项沿用单次消费的判定顺序，第一个失败项决定整批结果并回滚全部变更：已消费返回 409 grant_consumed，已紧急撤销返回 409 grant_revoked，已到或超过 expires_at 返回 409 grant_expired，其余合格授权在机器 suspended 时返回 409 machine_suspended。机器 suspended 时，已消费、已撤销或过期授权仍按前述高优先级状态报告。

批量消费必须与单次消费、撤销和机器状态变更并发一致。对任一授权，成功消费最多只有一个赢家；与单次消费或另一批量请求重叠时，失败方按输入顺序取得第一个竞争失败授权的上述唯一 409 状态，不得生成重复使用记录或留下部分消费。现有单次消费入口的响应、错误优先级、过期判定和恢复 active 后的语义不变，签发、撤销、审计、生命周期事件、执行回执、决策与证据链、异常、诊断、合规及隐私查询保持原行为。本功能只新增批量消费和必要的持久化使用记录，不改写历史数据。

1	"""One-time, short-lived authorization grants and their single consumption.
2	
3	A grant turns one already-committed, audit-passing *allow* decision event into
4	a short-lived credential that can be consumed exactly once:
5	
6	* :func:`issue_grant` accepts only an event of the path machine that committed
7	  ``allowed = true`` with ``reason = "allowed_by_policy"`` and whose immutable
8	  decision-basis snapshot passes the read-only consistency audit. The event,
9	  its basis, and the audit are read inside one locked write transaction, which
10	  also inserts the grant, so a concurrent burst signing for the same event has
11	  exactly one winner — a database-level unique constraint on ``event_id`` is
12	  the final backstop. Grants never modify the event, the basis, or any chain.
13	* :func:`issue_grants_batch` signs several qualified allow events into
14	  independent grants in one locked write transaction: every item is checked
15	  in input order against exactly the single-issue eligibility rules, the
16	  first failing item decides the whole batch's outcome, and a failure leaves
17	  no grant behind at all. A successful batch stamps every grant with the same
18	  UTC issue moment and its own ``ttl_seconds`` expiry.
19	* :func:`consume_grant` atomically flips one unused, unexpired, unrevoked
20	  grant to ``consumed`` and inserts its single use record in the same locked
21	  transaction, so a concurrent burst of consumptions has exactly one success;
22	  already-consumed, revoked, and expired grants are rejected and nothing is
23	  written. A grant that is still usable but belongs to a suspended machine is
24	  rejected with ``machine_suspended`` — after the not-found, consumed,
25	  revoked, and expired outcomes — and that rejection likewise writes nothing:
26	  the machine status change and the consumption take the same write lock, so
27	  whichever commits first decides, and the grant stays consumable again once
28	  the machine returns to ``active``.
29	* :func:`revoke_grant` performs the emergency revocation: it atomically flips
30	  one unused, unexpired, unrevoked grant to ``revoked`` and stamps
31	  ``revoked_at`` in the same kind of locked transaction, so a concurrent burst
32	  of revocations has exactly one winner and a revocation racing a consumption
33	  has one definite terminal winner — consume first makes the revocation answer
34	  ``grant_consumed``; revoke first makes the consumption answer
35	  ``grant_revoked``.
36	
37	Grants and use records live in their own tables and are never renewed,
38	transferred, or deleted. Revocation never touches the decision event, its
39	immutable basis, any hash chain, evidence, incident, diagnostic, or export. A
40	failed attempt writes neither the grant state change nor a use record: the
41	whole operation either commits together or leaves no trace.
42	
43	Every successful action also appends exactly one immutable lifecycle audit
44	event (``issued`` / ``consumed`` / ``revoked``) to the machine's
45	tamper-evident grant-lifecycle chain inside the same locked transaction
46	(:mod:`.grant_lifecycle`), reusing the response's own moment as the event's
47	``occurred_at``; a failed attempt appends no event.
48	"""
49	
50	import uuid
51	from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
52	from typing import Any
53	
54	from sqlalchemy import Engine, inspect, select, text
55	from sqlalchemy.exc import IntegrityError
56	
57	from . import decision_basis, decision_basis_integrity, grant_lifecycle
58	from .chain import _run_with_lock_retry
59	from .db import (
60	    AuthorizationDecisionEvent,
61	    AuthorizationGrant,
62	    AuthorizationGrantUse,
63	    Machine,
64	)
65	
66	_EVENT_TABLE = AuthorizationDecisionEvent.__table__
67	_GRANT_TABLE = AuthorizationGrant.__table__
68	_USE_TABLE = AuthorizationGrantUse.__table__
69	
70	
71	def migrate_schema(engine: Engine) -> None:
72	    """Add the revocation column to databases created before the feature."""
73	    inspector = inspect(engine)
74	    if _GRANT_TABLE.name not in inspector.get_table_names():
75	        # ``create_all`` builds a current-schema table; there is nothing to
76	        # bring forward.
77	        return
78	    existing = {
79	        column["name"]
80	        for column in inspector.get_columns(_GRANT_TABLE.name)
81	    }
82	    if "revoked_at" not in existing:
83	        with engine.begin() as conn:
84	            conn.execute(
85	                text(
86	                    f"ALTER TABLE {_GRANT_TABLE.name} "
87	                    "ADD COLUMN revoked_at VARCHAR"
88	                )
89	            )
90	
91	
92	def _utc_iso(instant: datetime) -> str:
93	    """Format an aware UTC instant as RFC 3339 text ending in ``Z``."""
94	    return instant.astimezone(timezone.utc).isoformat().replace("+00:00", "Z")
95	
96	
97	def _parse_utc(value: str) -> datetime:
98	    """Parse a stored ``Z``-suffixed UTC stamp back to an aware instant."""
99	    return datetime.fromisoformat(value.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
100	
101	
102	def issue_grant(
103	    engine: Engine,
104	    *,
105	    machine_id: str,
106	    event_id: str,
107	    ttl_seconds: int,
108	) -> dict[str, Any]:
109	    """Mint one one-time grant for one audit-passing allow event.
110	
111	    All reads, the eligibility checks, and the insert run in one locked write
112	    transaction. Returns a status dict:
113	
114	    * ``not_found`` — the path machine or the (path-machine scoped) event is
115	      missing or owned by another machine;
116	    * ``event_not_allowed`` — the event exists but did not commit
117	      ``allowed = true`` / ``reason = "allowed_by_policy"``;
118	    * ``decision_basis_unavailable`` — the event has no historical
119	      decision-basis snapshot (it predates the feature);
120	    * ``decision_basis_invalid`` — the snapshot exists but the read-only
121	      consistency audit rejects it;
122	    * ``grant_already_exists`` — the event already has a grant;
123	    * ``ok`` — with the new ``grant`` dict.
124	
125	    Nothing is written on any non-ok outcome.
126	    """
127	
128	    def _work(conn) -> dict[str, Any]:
129	        machine = conn.execute(
130	            Machine.__table__.select().where(Machine.__table__.c.id == machine_id)
131	        ).first()
132	        if machine is None:
133	            return {"status": "not_found"}
134	        event_row = conn.execute(
135	            _EVENT_TABLE.select().where(
136	                _EVENT_TABLE.c.id == event_id,
137	                _EVENT_TABLE.c.machine_id == machine_id,
138	            )
139	        ).first()
140	        if event_row is None:
141	            return {"status": "not_found"}
142	
143	        event = event_row._mapping
144	        # Only a committed policy allow may ever be signed into a grant.
145	        if not event["allowed"] or event["reason"] != "allowed_by_policy":
146	            return {"status": "event_not_allowed"}
147	
148	        document = decision_basis.load_document(
149	            conn, machine_id=machine_id, event_id=event_id
150	        )
151	        if document is None:
152	            # An event committed before the basis feature has no historical
153	            # basis: never reconstruct one from current data.
154	            return {"status": "decision_basis_unavailable"}
155	
156	        conclusion = decision_basis_integrity.verify(
157	            conn, machine_id=machine_id, event=event_row, document=document
158	        )
159	        if not conclusion["valid"]:
160	            return {"status": "decision_basis_invalid"}
161	
162	        existing = conn.execute(
163	            select(_GRANT_TABLE.c.id).where(_GRANT_TABLE.c.event_id == event_id)
164	        ).first()
165	        if existing is not None:
166	            return {"status": "grant_already_exists"}
167	
168	        issued = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
169	        issued_at = _utc_iso(issued)
170	        expires_at = _utc_iso(issued + timedelta(seconds=ttl_seconds))
171	        grant_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
172	        conn.execute(
173	            _GRANT_TABLE.insert().values(
174	                id=grant_id,
175	                machine_id=machine_id,
176	                event_id=event_id,
177	                issued_at=issued_at,
178	                expires_at=expires_at,
179	                status="active",
180	                consumed_at=None,
181	            )
182	        )
183	        # The audit event commits in the same locked transaction as the
184	        # grant, reusing the response's issued_at as its occurred_at.
185	        grant_lifecycle.append_event(
186	            conn,
187	            machine_id=machine_id,
188	            grant_id=grant_id,
189	            authorization_event_id=event_id,
190	            type="issued",
191	            occurred_at=issued_at,
192	        )
193	        return {
194	            "status": "ok",
195	            "grant": {
196	                "id": grant_id,
197	                "machine_id": machine_id,
198	                "event_id": event_id,
199	                "issued_at": issued_at,
200	                "expires_at": expires_at,
201	                "status": "active",
202	            },
203	        }
204	
205	    try:
206	        return _run_with_lock_retry(engine, _work)
207	    except IntegrityError:
208	        # The unique event_id constraint is the cross-backstop race guard: a
209	        # concurrent transaction that committed the first grant first wins.
210	        return {"status": "grant_already_exists"}
211	
212	
213	def issue_grants_batch(
214	    engine: Engine,
215	    *,
216	    machine_id: str,
